display.name: Modal
display.description: Modal serverless function health: input throughput and success rate, cold start, queue wait and execution time, container backlog and churn, per-function CPU and memory, and GPU saturation. Fed by Modal's workspace-level OpenTelemetry metrics integration.

display.name: Inputs Processed
display.description: Total function inputs Modal accepted over the selected range, summed across every matching function.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Success Rate
display.description: Successful inputs as a share of all inputs. Modal has no error-count metric, so this is successes / total_inputs.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name
environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Failed Inputs
display.description: Inputs that did not succeed, derived as total_inputs - successes. Modal does not emit a failure counter directly.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name
environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Running Containers
display.description: Containers currently running across the workspace. This tile ignores the Function selection on purpose: sandboxes and image builds leave function_name empty, so filtering by function would drop them from the count.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Input Throughput by Function
display.description: Inputs accepted per interval, per function. modal.input_events.* carries the module-qualified function name, for example modal_load.worker.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Successful vs Failed Inputs
display.description: Successes plotted against derived failures (total_inputs - successes) for the whole selection.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name
environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Failed Inputs by Function
display.description: Per-function failure count, derived as total_inputs - successes. Functions with no failures sit flat on zero.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.description: successes / total_inputs per function, as a percentage.

display.name: Cold Start Time (mean)
display.description: Mean cold start per function, computed as coldstart_time_us.sum / coldstart_time_us.count. The .bucket series carries only a +Inf boundary in this workspace, so true percentiles are not computable.

display.name: Cold Start Time (worst case)
display.description: Worst cold start Modal reported in each interval, from coldstart_time_us.max. Use this as the tail-latency stand-in, since the histogram has no usable buckets.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name

display.name: Input Queue Wait (mean)
display.description: Mean time an input waited before a container picked it up: input_queue_time_us.sum / .count. Rising queue wait with flat execution time means you are container-starved.

display.name: Backlog: Pending vs Running Inputs
display.description: Queued inputs plotted against in-flight inputs across the whole selection. Pending climbing while running is flat means Modal is not scaling containers fast enough. Not filtered by Function: modal.function.* reports the bare function name (worker) while every other metric reports the module-qualified name (modal_load.worker), so the two cannot share one filter.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type
environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Pending Inputs by Function
display.description: Queue depth per function. Uses the bare function name (worker), not the module-qualified name used elsewhere in this dashboard.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Running Inputs by Function
display.description: Inputs currently executing per function. Compare against Pending Inputs by Function to see which function owns the backlog.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Running Containers by Object Type
display.description: Container concurrency split into function containers, sandboxes and image builds. Sandboxes report container metrics only, never modal.input_events.* or modal.function.*.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Running Containers by App

display.name: Container Terminations by Reason
display.description: Container churn per interval, split by Modal's termination reason (for example finished, USER_CANCELLED). A rise in anything other than finished is worth investigating.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: Container Terminations by Object Type
display.description: Churn split into function containers, sandboxes and image builds. modal.container.terminations carries no function_name, so the Function variable does not narrow this panel.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type

display.name: CPU Utilisation by Function
display.description: Average CPU utilisation per function. Modal reports this as a fraction from 0 to 1, so 1.0 means one full core saturated.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name AND function_name EXISTS AND function_name != ''

display.name: Peak CPU Utilisation by Function
display.description: Busiest container per function in each interval. Averaging across containers hides a single hot container; this does not.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name AND function_name EXISTS AND function_name != ''

display.name: Memory Usage by Function
display.description: Peak resident memory per function, in bytes. modal.memory.utilization is deprecated, so this dashboard uses modal.memory.usage.

filter.expression: environment_name IN $environment_name AND app_name IN $app_name AND object_type IN $object_type AND function_name IN $function_name AND function_name EXISTS AND function_name != ''

display.name: Peak GPU Compute Utilisation
display.description: Busiest GPU in the selection, as a fraction from 0 to 1. Every Modal container emits the modal.gpu.* series and non-GPU containers report 0, so this panel aggregates with max rather than avg: the zeros cannot dilute the reading. Pin the Function variable to a GPU workload to drop the flat zero series entirely.

display.name: Object Type

display.description: Modal reports this key two ways. Container and modal.input_events.* metrics use the module-qualified name (modal_load.worker); modal.function.pending_inputs and modal.function.running_inputs use the bare name (worker). Panels driven by modal.function.* therefore ignore this variable, and so do the container-count and termination panels, where sandboxes and image builds leave function_name empty.
